statement: The standard error of a held-out R² on n rows is approximately 2·√R²·(1−R²)/√n (the delta-method large-sample variance of a squared correlation, for predictions calibrated on new rows), and at an assumed R² of 0.2 (a modest prediction R² for a diet outcome) ±1.96 SE is the precision a holdout of that size can deliver.

user_sees: "About {n} held-out rows: R² known to about ±0.xx." and "Widths are approximate 95% intervals … R² by its large-sample standard error 2·√R²·(1 − R²)/√n at an R² of 0.2 …"
claimed_basis: Delta-method derivation in the docstring; audit A19/E11; numpy simulation.
notes: The simulation checks only R² = 0.2, n ∈ {100, 500}, and true-signal predictions; it does not test the choice of 0.2 or miscalibrated models. PRECISION_NOTE at seal.py:616-619; PLAN_R2 at seal.py:606-608. | Inventory source id: F1-020.
